question: What is the typical length of a normal adult fallopian tube?
explanation: Normal fallopian tubes measure about 7 to 14 centimeters long, which is the perfect size to catch and transport eggs safely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h1)

question: If a patient has a shorter-than-normal fallopian tube, what are the two main ways this can happen?
explanation: Short tubes are either congenital (meaning present from birth due to development) or acquired later in life from things like scar tissue or surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h1)

question: Where does fertilization of the egg by the sperm normally take place in the female reproductive tract?
explanation: The ampulla is the wider middle section of the fallopian tube, providing just the right space for the sperm to meet and fertilize the egg. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h2)

question: What is the main job of the fimbriae (the finger-like ends of the fallopian tube)?

options.A: To produce progesterone to maintain early pregnancy
options.B: To nourish the sperm during capacitation
options.C: To catch the released oocyte from the ovary

explanation: Think of the fimbriae as little fingers that gently sweep over the ovary to catch the egg as soon as it's released during ovulation! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h2)

question: During embryonic development, which structures form the female reproductive tract, including the fallopian tubes?
explanation: The Müllerian ducts are the embryonic building blocks for the female reproductive system. If they don't develop quite right, it can lead to tubal or uterine variations. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h3)

question: Which of these is a common acquired (later in life) cause of a shortened fallopian tube?

options.B: Previous partial salpingectomy or pelvic surgery
options.D: Long-term use of oral contraceptive pills

explanation: If a part of the tube has to be surgically removed—like during treatment for an ectopic pregnancy—the overall length of the tube becomes shorter. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h3)

question: How does a shortened fallopian tube typically affect how a fertilized egg travels to the uterus?

options.A: It causes rapid transit, leading to early entry into the uterus
options.B: It traps the embryo permanently in the isthmus
options.C: It reverses the muscular waves pushing it backward
options.D: It completely stops all ciliary movement in the tubal lining

explanation: Because there is less distance to travel, the fertilized egg rushes through too quickly and reaches the uterus before it is fully ready to implant. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h4)

question: What is the main functional challenge when a patient has a congenitally shortened fallopian tube?

options.A: The time window for optimal gamete interaction and transport is compressed
options.B: Progesterone production by the tubal mucosa is permanently doubled
options.C: Sperm are completely blocked from entering the peritoneal cavity
options.D: Ovulation is prevented from occurring on the affected side

explanation: A shorter tube means less time and space for the delicate timing needed between sperm meeting the egg and the egg traveling down safely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h4)

question: How is a short fallopian tube most commonly discovered in a clinical setting?

options.A: Through routine screening blood tests for hormone levels
options.B: Because of chronic lower back pain and fever
options.C: During infertility workups or incidental pelvic imaging
options.D: During routine breast examination and palpation

explanation: Short tubes usually don't cause pain on their own. They are usually spotted when doctors investigate why a patient is having trouble conceiving, or during scans done for other reasons. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h5)

question: Why does a shortened fallopian tube raise the risk of an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: The fertilized egg implants inside the tube before reaching the uterus
options.B: Ovaries release eggs directly into the abdominal wall
options.C: Tubal smooth muscle completely loses its ability to contract
options.D: Sperm travel too slowly to reach the ampulla in time

explanation: Since the egg moves too fast and doesn't time its journey right, it can end up planting itself inside the tiny wall of the fallopian tube instead of the uterus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h5)

question: What is considered the gold standard procedure for directly viewing pelvic structures and measuring tubal length?
explanation: Laparoscopy lets the surgeon look directly inside the pelvis with a tiny camera, making it the best way to check out the fallopian tubes up close. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h6)

question: During a hysterosalpingography (HSG) procedure, what is injected into the uterus to make the tubes visible on an X-ray?
explanation: Doctors use a special contrast dye so that X-ray machines can clearly trace the fluid as it flows through the womb and down the fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h6)

question: Why is In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) often suggested for patients with damaged or very short fallopian tubes?

options.A: It lengthens the existing tube through hormone stimulation
options.B: It permanently cures any underlying pelvic infections
options.C: It prevents ovulation from happening on the damaged side
options.D: It completely bypasses the need for functional fallopian tubes

explanation: With IVF, fertilization happens in a lab, and the embryo is placed straight into the uterus—meaning healthy fallopian tubes aren't needed at all! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful medical or surgical option for managing tubal factor infertility?

options.A: Prolonged bed rest and pelvic massage

explanation: Bed rest and massages cannot fix structural problems or short lengths in the fallopian tubes. Medical treatments like IVF or surgery are needed for that. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h7)

question: As a nurse, what is a crucial warning sign of an ectopic pregnancy you must teach patients to report right away?

options.A: Mild generalized fatigue and mild morning nausea
options.B: Temporary swelling in the lower extremities
options.C: Clear and painless watery vaginal discharge
options.D: One-sided sharp pelvic pain with abnormal spotting

explanation: Sharp pain on just one side of the lower belly, paired with unusual bleeding, is a major red flag for an ectopic pregnancy that needs urgent care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h8)

question: A patient is scheduled for a hysterosalpingography (HSG). What is the most important preparatory action for the nurse to take?

options.A: Administer a cleansing enema to empty the entire colon
options.B: Explain the procedure steps and what kind of cramping sensation to expect
options.C: Instruct the patient to fast from solid food for twenty-four hours
options.D: Place an indwelling urinary catheter before the imaging begins

explanation: Preparation is all about calming nerves! Explaining what will happen and warning them about mild period-like cramps helps the patient feel safe and ready. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h8)
